title: Austin Infrastructure & City Contracts, 1909
summary:
• **Fire Equipment Purchases**: Council approved three bids for fire hose supplies, selecting W.H. Richardson & Co. and Frank Newman & Bro.'s offerings (totaling around $2,565), plus appropriated $4,555 for fire hose purchases to outfit the Austin Fire Department.

• **City Hall Improvements**: Accepted bids for concrete sidewalks, curbs, and gutters around City Hall, with J. Brueggemann winning the contract at $435.50 for walks and curbs, and Parkinson & Coppley selected for gutters at $82.50.

• **Bridge Keeper Election**: Held a competitive five-ballot election to fill a vacancy, ultimately electing J.C. Adrian as the new Bridge Keeper after other candidates were progressively dropped.

• **Storm Sewer Funding**: Approved emergency appropriations of $446.45 to cover overrun costs on the West 6th Street storm sewer project due to unforeseen hard excavation and material expenses.

• **Failed Railroad Track Change**: Blocked a proposal allowing the Austin Electric Railroad to change tracks on San Jacinto Street and other roads, with the measure failing 8-4 after initial approval of the expedited process.

Alderman Scott for the CityxPaving Committee presented the following communication from
the City Engineer.

Austin,Texas,Jany 18th 1909:
Hon Mayor and City Council,City of Austin,Texas. Gentlemen :

I hope to complete the West Sixth street storm sewer by the end of this week,or early next
week.The last appropriation,how-ever,was, for several reasons,too small,and I beg to ask
for an additional appropriationto cover the payrolls for the past two weeks,and this
week,including the hauling of gravel.These for the past two weeks amount to $ 325.45,and
for this week it will proba-bly amount to $ 120.00.Total $ 445.45 .There will be,in
addition, some material bills which can be covered when the work is wound up.
When the last report was made there were some large material bills which I had approved
,and which I believed had been deducted from the account,but which had not,so that my
estimate for the balance of the expense was too small.In addition I have found that the
exca-vation was unavoidably cost more than I estimated,on account of hard digging in heavy
clay,and in the last block a costing of stone had to be cut through .It was also
considered advisableto continue the 30"sewer to Colorado street instead of reducing it to
24"at Lav-raca.An ordinance has been prepared to cover the above appropri- -ation,which is
for labor already done,and amount estimated for this week for labor.

Yours very truly,
G S Iredell,City Engineer.
